recent_posts.title: Non-coding workflows you can run with Claude Code
recent_posts.summary: Claude Code can be used far beyond coding tasks. This covers several non-coding workflows: setting up a second brain with Obsidian and markdown files, generating product videos using the Remotion skill, building a multi-step research pipeline that cross-verifies claims, enabling video analysis via a 'Claude video' skill that extracts frames and transcripts, creating graphic designs and infographics with the canvas design skill, managing content systems with Notion MCP integration, and assigning Claude specialized roles like finance manager, teacher, legal adviser, or data analyst. Each workflow relies on a claude.md configuration file to guide Claude's behavior within the project context.

Best practices for structuring your claude.md file to improve AI coding agent performance
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to structuring your claude.md (or equivalent agent config) file for better AI coding performance. Key recommendations include: instructing Claude to think before coding and state assumptions, enforcing simplicity-first with a 200-line threshold, limiting surgical changes to only what was asked, defining verifiable success criteria per task, specifying non-default CLI tools, creating path-scoped rule files for monorepos, placing project description at the top, requiring real verification before marking tasks complete, and ordering instructions by priority (hard rules first). The guide also advises keeping the file under 300 lines and treating it as a living document that evolves with the project.

recent_posts.title: Why Claude Code beats Claude Design for UI generation
recent_posts.summary: Claude Design, Anthropic's new AI design tool, is argued to be mostly hype — essentially Claude Code repackaged with a design-focused interface. The real quality improvement in AI-generated designs comes from the Opus 4.7 model upgrade (especially its improved vision at 3.75MP vs 1.15MP), not the tool itself. Claude Design has significant practical drawbacks: strict weekly usage limits that run out after ~20 iterations even on max plans, basic Git integration limited to read-only, and no direct code output. Claude Code is presented as the superior alternative for designers — it produces real shippable code, supports full Git operations, integrates component libraries (shadcn, Aceternity), connects to MCP servers, and allows parallel agent workflows for exploring design variations. The impressive demos circulating on social media are largely based on pre-made prompt templates with video backgrounds, replicable by any capable agent.

recent_posts.title: How to manage context rot in Claude Code with a 1M token window
recent_posts.summary: Large context windows like Claude's 1M token limit introduce a problem called 'context rot', where model performance degrades well before the window is full — starting around 300–400K tokens. The post explains four failure modes: context pollution, goal drift, memory corruption, and decision inaccuracy. It then covers practical strategies to combat these issues: manually triggering compaction before the rot threshold with explicit instructions, using the clear command for fresh starts, combining compaction with structured JSON state files, periodically asking the agent to recap goals, delegating isolated tasks to sub-agents to keep the main context clean, and rewinding instead of re-prompting when mistakes occur.

recent_posts.title: Vibe coded apps built by non-developers that generated millions in revenue
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of vibe-coded apps built by non-developers using AI tools that generated significant revenue. Cases include Medv (healthcare, $400M+ revenue), Calai (AI calorie tracker, $2M/month), Wave AI (note-taking, $7M), Fly Peter (browser flight simulator, $500K/month), Trendfeed (marketing tool, $12K in 4 weeks), Aura (website templates, $15K MRR), Sleek (prompt-to-website, $10K MRR), and Siteshore (AI citation verifier, acquired). Common patterns: using Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor; breaking apps into small incremental prompts; outsourcing non-core functions to third-party services; leveraging social media for zero-cost marketing; and defining a clear ideal customer profile from day one.

recent_posts.title: Unusual Claude Code plugins that actually improve your workflow
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of unconventional but useful Claude Code plugins and skills shared by the open-source community. Covered tools include: 'P on Ping' for game-voice notifications when Claude finishes tasks or needs permissions; 'Dog Food' for adversarial browser-based bug and UX review; 'Caveman' for reducing token bloat by forcing terse responses; 'Git Time Travel' for navigating and analyzing git history; 'Premortem' for predicting future production bugs; 'Mutation Testing' for evaluating test suite strength; 'The Fool' for stress-testing ideas and plans; 'Reddit Fetch' for bypassing Reddit bot blocks using Gemini CLI; and 'Color Expert' for improving AI-generated UI color choices using 100+ reference files.

recent_posts.title: How the Claude Code adviser strategy saves tokens and improves results
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic's 'adviser strategy' for Claude Code uses Sonnet as the main executive agent for all code changes and tool calls, while Opus acts as a consultant only when Sonnet gets stuck. This approach outperforms Sonnet alone on benchmarks and costs significantly less than running Opus as the primary agent. Practical tests show it works well for simple-to-medium complexity apps, resolving stubborn bugs faster and saving tokens. However, limitations exist: Sonnet sometimes misjudges task complexity and skips consulting the adviser, and for large-scale or highly complex apps with many dependencies, using Opus directly as the main agent is still faster and more reliable.

recent_posts.title: How to set up Claude Code properly before building any app
recent_posts.summary: A workflow guide for setting up Claude Code before starting any project. Covers creating a PRD via a planner agent, writing a tailored claude.md file, configuring specialized agents (commit, refactoring, verification) and skills, connecting MCPs for external services, defining negative constraints, maintaining progress and learnings files, writing tests from specs rather than implementation, and planning for load testing and scalability. Emphasizes that traditional software development processes remain essential but now serve to structure AI agents rather than human developers.

recent_posts.title: How to reduce Claude Code token usage and extend your rate limits
recent_posts.summary: Claude Code's rate limits are being hit faster than expected due to token bloat from truncated responses, oversized claude.md files, and background processes. Practical optimizations include using the clear, compact, rewind, and 'by the way' commands to manage context size, keeping claude.md under 300 lines with only project-specific guidance, splitting rules into path-specific files, disabling unused MCPs and background processes like automemory, configuring hooks to filter unnecessary output (e.g. passing test results), setting effort levels and model choice (Haiku/Sonnet over Opus for simpler tasks), enabling prompt caching, and controlling max output tokens.
